ai.description: This skink reaches 12 cm total length. It is golden-brown with distinct dark longitudinal stripes along the body. It features a slender, elongated form and a long, tapering tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Riopa lineata* from similar skinks by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark longitudinal stripe running along each side of its body.
ai.habitat: The Lined Supple Skink inhabits moist deciduous forests and leaf litter in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Lined Supple Skink is primarily crepuscular, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and soil during the cooler hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Riopa lineata* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Riopa lineata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
